candidates.title: Stellantis says tariffs, consumer demand driving weeks-long layoffs at Windsor plant
candidates.description: Global carmaker Stellantis says tariffs and consumer demand in North America are driving weeks-long layoffs at the company's plant in Windsor, Ont.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge in fatal N.L. case questions whether impaired driving sentences are working
candidates.description: A St. John's judge is questioning whether or not punishments are fitting the crime when it comes to impaired driving. Judge Bruce Short sentenced a man to five years in prison on Friday for a fatal crash in 2023.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: No Canadians elected to world hockey governing body; Turkey, New Zealand represented
candidates.description: Hockey Canada president and chief executive officer Katherine Henderson was up for one of the minimum three female spots on the IIHF council at Friday's election, but was eliminated in the second of three rounds of voting in Tenerife, Spain. That means no Canadians have been elected to the council, a surprising result for a nation considered one of the sport's powerhouses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Legal battles mount over the off-reserve Millennium Scoop
candidates.description: Courts countrywide are grappling with the complex question of whether federal and provincial governments can be sued for the stark overrepresentation of Indigenous children in the off-reserve child welfare system, delivering dizzyingly mixed results.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Actor and advocate Michael J. Fox promoted to companion level in Order of Canada
candidates.description: Spectators stood and applauded Michael J. Fox at Rideau Hall on Friday as Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour officially named the celebrated actor and Parkinson's disease activist to the companion level of the Order of Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Government inspection at 3 Ontario career colleges reported 'serious concerns,' court records show
candidates.description: Ontario government officials who inspected three Academy of Learning career colleges found evidence suggesting third parties were completing the coursework and a few students who couldn't name their school or program, they alleged in reports filed in court.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: It's the biggest Alberta separatist account on the internet. It has links to a movement leader
candidates.description: The account Rise of Alberta is anonymous and drives four times as much engagement as the next most popular account.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman in fake nurse case once again avoids sentencing after 6th postponement
candidates.description: Lisa Driscoll didn't show up to court on Thursday for what was supposed to be her long-awaited sentencing hearing. Lucky for her, the judge wasn't there either.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Michael J. Fox promoted within Order of Canada
candidates.description: Famed actor Michael J. Fox has been promoted to companion of the Order of Canada, the highest level within the order. The Order of Canada is meant to recognize people who make 'extraordinary contributions to the nation,' according to the Governor General of Canada website. Fox is also a vocal advocate in raising awareness for people living with Parkinson's disease. The actor went public with news he had Parkinson's in 1998 and is a co-founder of the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Niagara Falls returns Buffalo, N.Y., love with invite to red-white-blue falls display on Ontario side
candidates.description: Niagara Falls Tourism has placed a full-page open letter in a Buffalo newspaper, inviting Americans to cross the bridge and celebrate with Canadians on Saturday, including witnessing Niagara Falls light up in the Bills' red, white and blue colours. The latest gesture in the face of the trade war comes after the NFL team played Canada's anthem at the recent home opener.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Labrador primary school principal resigns, citing understaffing and increased demands
candidates.description: Parents held a rally after the school closed for the day when 20 teachers called in sick, after principal Ashley Barrett said staffing shortages were so dire that she did not feel she could make decisions that "protect student safety, well being and the quality of their education. "
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 2 horses named in memory of Johnny Gaudreau running in the same race
candidates.description: On Saturday, the two horses named after the beloved former Calgary Flame — Johnny Hockey and Gaudreau — will run in the same race at Belmont Park in New York.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornwall mayoral hopeful's candidacy in limbo over 'malicious' paperwork complaint
candidates.description: The ballots for this month's municipal election in Cornwall, Ont., have already been printed, but whether electors will actually be able to vote for one of the four candidates for mayor is now mired in uncertainty.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Black vulture, rarely seen in Canada, 'all the buzz' in Mayo, Yukon
candidates.description: Cameron Eckert, president of the Yukon Bird Club, wasted no time in deciding to make the five-hour drive from Whitehorse to Mayo to see the unusual visitor. The last time a black vulture was reported in the Yukon was in the 1980s, he said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Amid the push to build Canadian, a Quebec train factory is booming
candidates.description: A Quebec train factory battered by years of layoffs is expanding as governments push to buy Canadian. Alstom's La Pocatière plant is hiring and scaling up for major domestic rail contracts, including a $4.7-billion VIA Rail project.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gas plant fire east of Calgary leaves 1 in life-threatening condition
candidates.description: One person is in life-threatening condition after an industrial fire broke out at the Canadian Natural Resources Limited (CNRL) Hussar gas plant east of Calgary Friday morning, EMS says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Camper bitten by Cape Breton coyote recounts moments leading up to attack
candidates.description: Alex Radu says he was bikepacking the Cabot Trail over the course of a week and that the 15-second encounter he had with a coyote doesn't define what was mostly a "peaceful experience" at the Cape Breton Highlands National Park.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CBC/Radio-Canada reveals PWHL broadcast schedule, league announces playoff expansion
candidates.description: CBC/Radio-Canada unveiled its broadcast schedule Friday for the upcoming Professional Women’s Hockey League season, which features more games on the network than ever before.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What Cornell's alleged rape case and the Hockey Canada trial's striking parallels reveal
candidates.description: Several legal experts note there are some striking similarities between the alleged gang rape case unfolding at Cornell University this week and last year's Hockey Canada sexual assault trial in London, Ont., which saw all five players acquitted.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, amid energy crunch
candidates.description: The release would begin immediately and take four months, starting with a "substantial" diesel release within the first 20 days. Diesel prices have soared globally due to the oil supply crunch brought on by fighting in the Middle East between the U.S. and Iran.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CBS Sports describes Tony Romo's permanent exit as mutual parting
candidates.description: CBS Sports and Tony Romo have officially parted ways, one month after the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback pleaded no contest to charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'I was fighting for my life': Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls FlyDubai cockpit attack
candidates.description: The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 deaths amid violence and mistrust
candidates.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has recorded more than 4,000 deaths, authorities say, as they struggle to contain the spread of the virus.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornell 7: Governor vows to change N.Y. rape law that makes reporting hard when intoxication present
candidates.description: New York's governor and attorney general were set to give an update Friday morning about the investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house beginning at 9:30 a.m. ET.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard speaks out about death of her ex-fiancé, Ken Urker
candidates.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard, who spent more than seven years in prison for her mother's murder, is speaking out after Ken Urker, her former fiancé and the father of her daughter, died yesterday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Prepared ourselves for the worst': FlyDubai passenger recounts moments during cockpit attack
candidates.description: Almog Italie and his family were on the final leg of their trip home following a vacation in Japan when they felt FlyDubai flight FZ1073 plummet. Italie was one of 174 people on board the plane earlier this week when one of the pilots stabbed the other in an attempt to crash the plane. The flight plunged 30,000 feet in under 30 seconds.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The Black Sea is the most dangerous it's been since the start of Russia’s war. And it's choking global grain
candidates.description: Strikes against ports and vessels have crippled shipping routes leaving Russia's and Ukraine's combined wheat exports down by 60 per cent over last year. Global wheat prices are already up from a year ago, and experts warn it could get worse.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In Gaza, a UN cash-for-work program gives Palestinians some income — and hope
candidates.description: The UN World Food Program's cash-for-work program helps provide stable work and income for Palestinians in Gaza, who have with little to no other options.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Macron government struggles to quell protests as riot police clash with high schoolers
candidates.description: Riot police clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly ‌violent protests over classroom conditions and funding.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack
candidates.description: The motivations of a FlyDubai pilot, and what weapon was used, are among the foremost questions surrounding how a flight bound for Israel from the United Arab Emirates avoided disaster Wednesday after a cockpit incident.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New York's governor removes district attorney from Cornell rape allegations case, appoints special prosecutor
candidates.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor Thursday to oversee an investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house, with the governor saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney's ability to handle the case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Renee Good's family sues U.S. government, ICE officer and others over Minneapolis killing
candidates.description: Lawsuits filed by Renee Good's family allege wrongful death, conspiracy and other violations in the 37-year-old's fatal shooting by a U.S. immigration officer during an immigration crackdown in January.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What happened in Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike and what comes next?
candidates.description: It remains unclear why the execution of Christa Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of a classmate at age 18, failed. Pike was given two doses of lethal injections Wednesday, according to observers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Putin warns West not to escalate, claims concerns about Russia's Kaliningrad region
candidates.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff ‌over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it would defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.A.E. announces investigation into FlyDubai stabbing
candidates.description: The United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has ordered an investigation into the ‌stabbing aboard FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, ​which was diverted ​and landed in Saudi Arabia after a struggle ​in the cockpit, the state news agency ‌reported Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This is how fast Swiss glaciers, the 'water tower of Europe,' are melting away
candidates.description: Glaciers in Switzerland lost 5.5 per cent of their ice volume this year, the second-biggest percentage drop on record. It's part of a trend that could have big impacts in a country reliant on hydropower and which acts as the 'water tower of Europe,' feeding its major rivers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennessee governor orders outside review after death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt
candidates.description: Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a classmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, prison officials and her lawyers said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Families of Canadian mining firm workers kidnapped in Mexico plan to file RCMP complaint
candidates.description: The families of the workers of a Canadian mining firm kidnapped earlier this year by a suspected cartel commando squad in the violence-torn Mexican state of Sinaloa plan to file an RCMP complaint against the Vancouver-based company, their lawyer says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says 'very bad' Canada is being 'taught a little lesson' as trade action escalates
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's war of words with Canada continued Wednesday as he veered off a prepared script at an event marking Hispanic Heritage Month in the States to chastise Canadian leaders for being what he called "very bad."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: West Coast oil pipeline becomes 1st project designated in national interest
candidates.description: The federal and Alberta governments have announced that a proposed pipeline carrying one million barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the B.C. coast has become the first project designated in the national interest.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI agents tried to hack Library and Archives Canada website, research firm says
candidates.description: AI agents tried to hack into a Library and Archives Canada website, according to a report by artificial intelligence research firm Transluce.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Overnight, Meta deleted all her accounts. AI customer service won’t let her reach a human
candidates.description: Toronto resident Jasmine Ault says Meta disabled her accounts overnight, without giving her a reason, and that she's been unable to get past their AI chatbots to speak to a human to resolve the error. Experts say without regulation enforcing the right to speak to a human, this will keep happening.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
candidates.description: The woman, known as Jane Doe, alleges she was raped by seven students at a fraternity house at the university in 2024.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
candidates.description: Capt Smit Machchhar tells Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi he opened the cockpit door to let others in during the attack.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
candidates.description: The defeat raises pressure on Sánchez to call a snap election, after a series of scandals affecting his party and allies.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
candidates.description: Texas reporter Michael Graczyk has seen botched executions in his time, but not one in which an inmate survived.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'
candidates.description: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
candidates.description: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
candidates.description: "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power," says the former chess world champion.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Algeria introduces death penalty for arsonists after deadly wildfires
candidates.description: It is estimated more than 200 people have died in blazes in the north-east of the country over the summer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Explosions heard in Ethiopia's capital after drone flights banned
candidates.description: It comes a week after fighting erupted north of the capital between the army and a new alliance of armed groups.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump's AI rebrand causes 'unprecedented' demand for Slovenian website names
candidates.description: The president wants AI to be called super intelligence - or SI - the same initials used by Slovenian domains.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kanye West's Russia shows officially cancelled after weeks of uncertainty
candidates.description: Chaos has surrounded the St Petersburg shows since the stadium said it had not agreed to host the rapper.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: K-pop star convicted of violating military service law
candidates.description: The member of K-pop band Winner was given a suspended prison sentence for repeated absences from his national service work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: School protests send shivers down French government's spine
candidates.description: A movement that started nearly two weeks ago has spread, and in France young people on the streets spells trouble, writes Hugh Schofield.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
candidates.description: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election
candidates.description: A voter mobilisation campaign has registered huge numbers of young people but it is not clear who they are backing.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What we know about Christa Pike’s condition after failed execution
candidates.description: The BBC’s Ione Wells reports from outside the Tennessee hospital where Pike is said to have arrived Wednesday night after surviving two lethal injection attempts.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Cornell students voice frustration at public hearing over rape case
candidates.description: The BBC's Nada Tawfik was at the hearing, where the university's Student Assembly led a discussion around safety concerns and sexual violence on campus.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why are these endangered moths swarming Australia's east coast?
candidates.description: The sudden influx of Bogong moths has caused a stir in cities like Sydney and Canberra, with people filming them infiltrating their homes and cars.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI boom could trigger market shocks, Bank of England boss warns
candidates.description: Andrew Bailey says the central bank is watching the waves of cash being invested in artificial intelligence "very carefully".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest
candidates.description: Will farmers want AI tools to help judge when to pick fruit, or is their own intuition enough?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
candidates.description: The world-famous Palm House at the Royal Botanic Gardens Kew in London is about to undergo a massive makeover.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower this weekend
candidates.description: Friday sees the start of the Orionid meteor shower as Earth passes through debris left behind by Halley’s Comet. It peaks later in October.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: SpaceX launches crew to ISS
candidates.description: The Falcon 9 rocket blasted off from Cape Canaveral with two Americans, a Russian and a Canadian who will spend up to six months aboard the International Space Station.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The G7 will release 100 million reserve barrels of diesel fuel over the next 4 months
candidates.description: After increased pressure from Washington, the G7 held an emergency meeting on energy. The world's wealthiest nations say they will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel in their reserves.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Germany's political center fights for relevance after far-right and far-left gains
candidates.description: Centrist politicians are soul-searching after electoral gains by the far right and the far left. Today's weak coalitions, political fragmentation and dire economy echo a past that led to the rise of fascism.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
candidates.description: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Cloaked in anonymity, Israeli soldiers describe mass civilian killings in 'NAZA'
candidates.description: NAZA is an acronym for nezek agavi , Hebrew for "collateral damage." It refers to the number of civilian casualties the Israeli military deems acceptable. The documentary is made by Israeli filmmakers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Cornell rape case gets special prosecutor. And, Renee Good's family sues the government
candidates.description: New legal action in two closely watched cases: one at Cornell, the other over Renee Good's death. We take a closer look.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pro-democracy activists increasingly vulnerable to authoritarian governments in Southeast Asia
candidates.description: Activists across Asia are being hunted down by authoritarian governments even across international borders. Human rights groups have been warning of a "swap market" of repression in Southeast Asia.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
candidates.description: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
candidates.description: What we know so far about the tense moments aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flight. And, the FBI investigates a cyberattack involving sensitive employee data.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel's prime minister says a pilot tried to crash a plane traveling to Tel Aviv
candidates.description: One pilot stabbed another pilot on a FlyDubai flight headed to Tel Aviv on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the plane before passengers and crew members subdued him, Israel's prime minister says.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
candidates.description: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pro-Trump Influencer Benny Johnson is being sued for defamation by ICE protesters
candidates.description: The lawsuit says the prominent conservative podcaster falsely claimed the protesters were assaulting ICE officers during demonstrations at an ICE facility in Illinois last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
candidates.description: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why is diesel more expensive than regular gas?
candidates.description: Diesel hasn't always been more expensive than other gasoline. Then in 2004, a switch happened due to air quality standards, demand, and taxes. In this week's Indicator newsletter, we dig into diesel prices, what kind of fun people are buying, and other forms of making your tax bill smaller.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
candidates.description: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
candidates.description: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Breweries adapt as tastes in beer change
candidates.description: The craft beer market is saturated and tastes are changing. Brewers are coming with innovative ways to attract customers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Google launches Project Suncatcher, a step towards AI data centers in space
candidates.description: The fridge-size satellite with AI chips on board is part of Project Suncatcher, the company's moonshot effort to put AI data centers in space and harness solar energy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Egg prices have tumbled since Trump returned to office. Here's why
candidates.description: Agriculture experts say high egg prices were the result of severe avian flu outbreaks, but the Trump administration's tariffs and the war with Iran have also put pressure on farmers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trade tensions mean fewer Canadians flocking to South Florida
candidates.description: This South Florida community is typically a refuge for Canadians fleeing cold weather, but trade tensions between the United States and Canada mean fewer are coming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
candidates.description: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
candidates.description: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
candidates.description: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump administration reverses stance on integration of people with disabilities
candidates.description: Disability rights advocates are angered by the latest reversal but are rallying behind proposed legislation and working with states to strengthen protections for community integration.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: * WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust. Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted air quality levels. * WHERE...In Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on emissions and local weather conditions. * WHEN...Oct 3 6AM to Midnight. * IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.

candidates.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
candidates.description: 3D Gaussian avatars support fast rendering, however, their real-time animation is often challenged by the costly neural inference. We address this bottleneck and show that the animation of pretrained avatar models can be closely approximated by a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes. Building on this finding, we introduce GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a shallow coefficient predictor and a linear blend. To improve fidelity and reduce memory requirements, we propose to construct the basis using block-local PCA under a rendering-aware metric and a memory budget. Our method learns a shallow MLP network to predict blendshape coefficients and applies to various animation architectures without retraining original models. We validate GALA by accelerating the inference of three distinct avatar models for 3D animation of facial expressions and full-bodies with clothing dynamics. Across these models, our distillation generalizes to held-out identities and reduces CPU animation cost by up to three orders of magnitude while preserving most of the rendering quality. Excellent results of our method confirm the shared linear structure of learned avatar representations and enable highly efficient and accurate animation at frame rates reaching up to 60fps on mobile devices. Project page: https://ramazan793.github.io/gala/
candidates.author: Ramazan Fazylov, Stamatis Lefkimmiatis, Ivan Laptev

candidates.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
candidates.description: LLMs are increasingly applied to cybersecurity workflows, where they are expected to translate analysts' intent into tool invocations. However, existing evaluations focus on knowledge-based assessments or end-to-end agentic tasks, and do not directly measure LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools. This gap is critical because cybersecurity operations rely on strict command-line interfaces (CLIs), where minor syntax errors, incorrect flag--value bindings, or argument misordering can invalidate execution. We introduce KaliBench, a fine-grained benchmark and dataset for natural-language--to--CLI translation on Kali Linux, comprising 8,504 query--command pairs spanning 1,642 tools across 23 capability dimensions and 5 security phases. KaliBench is constructed via a manuscript-grounded pipeline with deterministic canonicalization and alias-aware evaluation, enabling precise and reproducible assessment of tool selection and argument construction. To ensure both semantic correctness and practical executability, we develop a multi-stage verification pipeline that combines LLM-based validation, sandboxed terminal execution, and human-in-the-loop refinement. Building on these fine-grained, deterministic signals, KaliBench further enables runtime-free verifiable rewards for training. Across three evaluation modes and 24 configurations of general-purpose and security-focused open-weight models, no open-weight model exceeds 42% exact-command accuracy in the unrestricted setting, highlighting the difficulty of accurate CLI-based cybersecurity tool use without explicit tool hints. We further show that supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards derived from KaliBench significantly improve an 8B model and achieve performance comparable to a 685B MoE model.
candidates.author: Pengfei Li, Naufal Suryanto, Sicheng Zhang, Muzammal Naseer

candidates.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
candidates.description: Building reliable robot capabilities across diverse tasks requires substantial human effort to develop and maintain skills, design rewards, and integrate perception with control. We present Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real (RPG), a framework for autonomous improvement of robot execution systems without updating model weights. RPG identifies manipulation capabilities in an offline dataset and constructs related practice tasks in simulation. During practice, RPG uses execution feedback, privileged simulator state, and available dataset videos to diagnose failures. It develops new reusable symbolic skills, refines existing skills, and revises the system prompt based on these diagnoses. Cross-task evaluation tests individual candidate changes and merged revisions before they are retained for reuse. At test time, a multimodal LLM uses the resulting system prompt and skill library to coordinate perception and robot control. On held-out initializations of 22 manipulation tasks, RPG improves task success from 28.6% after the first practice round to 95.0% after 15 rounds, outperforming all evaluated baselines, including ASPIRE (75.5%) and CaP-Agent0 powered by GPT-6 Astra Pro (60.0%). After a common calibration and hardware-adaptation procedure, the frozen system succeeds in all 30 physical trials, with ten trials on each of three tasks. Project Website: https://rpg-robot.github.io/
candidates.author: Yen-Jen Wang, Haozhe Jiang, Shuying Deng, Haoru Xue, Weirui Ye, Rocky Duan, Nika Haghtalab, S. Shankar Sastry, Pieter Abbeel, Haozhi Qi

candidates.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
candidates.description: What makes great scientists great? Even as AI systems start to make progress on open problems, scientists remain far ahead of them at sensing which prior idea, buried in an ever-growing archive of research, a new problem needs. To study this skill, we draw on researchers who know firsthand which earlier work advanced their completed projects, with papers serving as pointers to the ideas within. Using our automated pipeline that makes author annotation scalable, we build ScholarCatalyst by having 184 lead authors of 207 recent computer science papers label which candidates did or could have advanced their project, each with a detailed rationale. We introduce a retrieval task with author-provided judgments: given an initial research question, retrieve these papers from only the literature available when the project began. Agentic search does no better than embedding retrieval (0.42 vs. 0.48 Recall@20) despite calling that same retriever as a tool. Even an agent built on Claude Fable 5.1, which may have seen the completed papers during training, reaches only 0.51 R@20. These results highlight the need for new training recipes that equip models with expert intuition for searching broad corpora. We envision ScholarCatalyst as a step toward scientific agents that can take a half-formed idea and point to the prior research it needs.
candidates.author: Sohyeon Kim, Yoonho Lee, Bo Liu, Dayoon Ko, Rulin Shao, Seungone Kim, Graham Neubig, Pang Wei Koh, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Akari Asai, Omar Khattab, Yejin Choi, Gunhee Kim, Chelsea Finn

candidates.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
candidates.description: High-resolution 3D generation increasingly relies on voxel latents and multi-stage pipelines that first predict active structure and then synthesize local geometry. While effective, this design fragments continuous surfaces into many local tokens, inflates generation cost, and often weakens topological consistency for thin or highly connected shapes. We introduce SILSA, a topology-aware 3D generation framework that represents shapes with compact sliding-window slice latents. Instead of generating expensive voxel tokens, SILSA uses a fixed set of overlapping slices along the three canonical axes, where each token summarizes a local depth window to preserve cross-sectional continuity and support single-stage rectified-flow generation. A Slice VAE encodes oriented surface samples into multi-axis slice latents and reconstructs them with a sparse volumetric decoder, while a Volumetric Anchor Lattice coordinates directional slice streams through a shared 3D workspace. To preserve structural correctness, we introduce slice-level topology supervision that matches persistence diagrams and aligns Betti transitions across neighboring slices. Experiments show that SILSA improves structural fidelity while substantially reducing generation cost. SILSA improves PSNR by $8.7\%$, coverage by $5.96$ absolute points, and Betti error by $9.2\%$ over the strongest baseline, while using $70.0\%$ fewer tokens than the next-most compact baseline and over $98\%$ fewer tokens than sparse or hierarchical tokenizers, effectively reducing training memory by $40.4\%$ and inference time by $58.5\%$. Qualitative results further show improved preservation of thin structures, repeated components, and long-range connectivity.
candidates.author: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen, Adheesh Sunil Juvekar, Ismini Lourentzou

candidates.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
candidates.description: We show that multimodal models possess strong reasoning abilities and that an appropriate harness can unlock their potential to solve tasks across diverse interactive environments. We introduce VISTA, a visual harness that gives a general-purpose multimodal model long-horizon vision. VISTA allows the model to directly perceive the environment through visual observations and maintains a lossless visual memory that preserves past observations in their original form. The model can actively retrieve these observations and reorganize its visual input as it reasons. On ARC-AGI-3, VISTA improves Claude Opus 5.0's Relative Human Action Efficiency score from 40.68 to a perfect 100.00, with the model completing all 25 public games using 57.4% fewer actions than first-time human participants. VISTA's simple design also allows it to extend naturally to diverse visual environments with minimal adaptation. Across three additional benchmarks covering a diverse range of visual games and puzzles, it substantially outperforms baselines using the same underlying model with minimal harnesses. Our results highlight VISTA's potential as a general-purpose visual harness for advancing multimodal agents in complex visual environments.
candidates.author: Qiushi Han, Keya Hu, Linlu Qiu, Cathy Wu, Kaiming He

candidates.title: FERPO: Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization
candidates.description: Several state-of-the-art methods for online reinforcement learning in continuous control improve policies using action gradients of a learned critic. However, critics are typically trained to predict returns, and accurate value predictions do not necessarily yield accurate action derivatives, potentially leading to unreliable policy updates. We propose Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization (FERPO), an on-policy maximum entropy reinforcement learning algorithm that performs policy improvement using critic values without differentiating the critic with respect to actions. FERPO derives an optimal target action distribution from a policy-improvement objective regularized by entropy and Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. We then fit the actor to this target by minimizing a forward-KL objective, estimated using self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS) with actions drawn from the rollout policy. By limiting the target distribution's deviation from the rollout policy, the KL regularization helps keep these importance weights well behaved. In contrast to reverse-KL objectives, which can favor a subset of the target distribution's modes, the forward-KL objective encourages coverage of multiple high-value modes and thereby promotes exploration. Experiments and ablations on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill show competitive performance and sample-efficiency gains. Computational benchmarks also demonstrate faster actor updates than Relative Entropy Pathwise Policy Optimization (REPPO).
candidates.author: Sebastian Sanokowski, Alireza Sarmadi, Majid Khadiv

candidates.title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.description: We study test-time evolution for humanoid loco-manipulation: solving tasks that a controller was never trained for by repurposing its existing skills, improving from its own attempts, and retaining what it learns, without retraining. Our key insight is that a broad controller already holds much of the competence a new task needs, and that this competence becomes accessible through an interface between planning and control that is expressive enough to specify contact-rich, multi-stage interactions, yet executable and measurable enough that execution feedback can guide planning from experience. InterEvolve realizes this interface with two components. First, we develop an object-aware forward-backward (FB) behavioral foundation model, whose object residuals on a frozen body prior turn a new reward about the body or objects into loco-manipulation behavior at test time. Second, we specify tasks as reward programs: staged rewards with completion conditions and tunable constants. A large language model (LLM) agent revises the program structure in context, drawing on execution feedback and a skill library of verified programs, while a numerical optimizer tunes its constants. With every candidate verified across parallel simulation scenarios, the program explores new ways to induce, repurpose, and compose the controller's existing motor competence for the task at hand, and thus improves over iterations. Experiments show that human-designed rewards leave much of the FB model's loco-manipulation competence untapped, whereas the programs InterEvolve evolves release it, sometimes through novel strategies. It further produces behaviors for diverse tasks, complex scenes, and long-horizon compositions in simulation, and evolved skills run autonomously on a physical Unitree G1 from egocentric onboard perception.
candidates.author: Zhuo Lin, Sirui Xu, Liuyu Bian, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

candidates.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
candidates.description: Discrete diffusion language models offer a compelling alternative to autoregressive generation for tasks demanding bidirectional reasoning and global constraint satisfaction. Yet they share a structural bottleneck: when decoding in parallel, each token is sampled independently from its marginal, severing the statistical dependencies among the tokens decoded together. Continuous diffusion language models avoid this by denoising a shared continuous state, but their denoiser sees only that state, so nothing ties it to a valid token configuration until it is finally decoded. To address this, we propose Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models (HC-DLM), which couple discrete token generation with a continuous latent trajectory in a single, principled denoising process, whose training objective is derived from a variational bound on the token likelihood. In contrast to recent methods that attach continuous context to a self-contained discrete chain, HC-DLM makes the latent the only persistent generative state: tokens are read out from it at every step and feed back as a scaffold for the next latent update. On structured reasoning (Sudoku), mathematical planning (Countdown) and language modeling (LM1B), HC-DLM improves over discrete and continuous diffusion baselines at matched model size, in puzzle accuracy on Sudoku and Countdown and in generative perplexity on LM1B. Project page: https://hc-dlm.github.io/.
candidates.author: Hui Ren, Zihan Li, Chang Liu, Huidong Liu, Alexander Schwing

candidates.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
candidates.description: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) trains a few-step student from the difference between separately estimated target and student scores, so it must keep an auxiliary diffusion model fitted to the student's evolving distribution at extra memory and computation cost. We introduce DMAD, Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation, which recasts distribution matching as classification and learns the required log-density ratios directly. Two discriminator heads on a shared backbone distinguish real data and teacher samples from the student's, and linear losses on their logits train the student without auxiliary score fitting. We prove that at the discriminator optimum these losses recover the distribution-matching gradient underlying DMD, through the classical identity linking discriminator logits to log-density ratios. We further introduce gap-based reweighting, which adapts teacher supervision across noise levels from the real-data head's empirical logit gap between real and teacher samples. DMAD reaches a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 1.04 with one-step generation on ImageNet-64x64, 14.47 with four-step SDXL on COCO-10K, and a VBench total score of 85.15 with four-step Wan2.1-T2V-14B, the best values among the compared few-step methods and the multi-step teachers. On MiniMax-H3-33B, our four-step student achieves overall human preference rates of 79.1% over DMD2 and 84.6% over rCM for joint audio-video generation, excluding ties. Our code, models and demos are available at https://yzmblog.github.io/projects/DMAD.
candidates.author: Zhengming Yu, Junkun Yuan, Haotian Yang, Gordon Guocheng Qian, Yizhi Wang, Angtian Wang, Yiding Yang, Bo Liu, Xin Li, Wenping Wang, Chongyang Ma

candidates.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
candidates.description: Molecular learning models are strongly shaped by their underlying representations. Yet standard sequential and graph formalisms struggle to explicitly encode higher-order topology, such as ring systems and recurring motifs. Existing higher-order representations can capture these structures directly, but they are often computationally demanding and difficult to decode into valid molecules. Here, we introduce Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR), a principled, topology-aware framework that lifts molecules to combinatorial complexes and parses each complex into a compact sequence of production rules under a context-free higher-order grammar. By serialising higher-order topology into rule sequences, HGR makes these structures directly compatible with standard sequence models, avoiding the computational overhead of explicit higher-order encodings while preserving topological expressiveness. To reduce benchmark bias towards simple ring systems, we construct RingDiv, a ring-enriched benchmark containing 1.18 million molecules, including the curated RingDiv300k subset, and introduce the ring diversity index (RDI) to quantify ring-system coverage. In molecular generation, HGR-based models uniquely combine 100% validity by construction with leading distributional alignment, ranking first in FCD on all five generation benchmarks. In representation learning, HGR-FM achieves the highest mean AUC across seven MoleculeNet benchmarks under both transfer protocols, improving on the strongest baseline by 8.3 and 3.3 AUC points under probing and full fine-tuning, respectively. Collectively, these results establish HGR as an efficient higher-order representation for molecular generation and transferable representation learning.
candidates.author: Yiming Huang, Yujie Zeng, Vijay Prakash Dwivedi, Simone Foti, Jianmin Wang, Jure Leskovec, Tolga Birdal

candidates.title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
candidates.description: Quasi-Newton (QN) methods have long been among the most effective methods for large-scale unconstrained convex optimization. Two obstacles have limited their use in deep learning: non-convexity and enormous parameter sizes. We introduce SoftServe, a family of QN methods designed to overcome these obstacles without line searches or ad hoc curvature corrections. SoftServe derives positivedefinite curvature estimates from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025), even in the presence of negative curvature. We develop diagonal and Kroneckerfactored variants that preserve positive definiteness by construction and scale to massive neural networks. Finally, SoftServe relies on the stable coupled Newton-Schulz iteration for the required matrix operations, replacing costly matrix decompositions with GPU-friendly matrix multiplications. SoftServe excels on problems that are severely ill-conditioned, including tasks such as recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model, often achieving lower losses than established baselines including Adam, Muon, and SOAP.
candidates.author: Joohwan Ko, Tetiana Parshakova, Diana Cai, Robert M. Gower
